sections.title: 🌊 Open Sea Overview & Key Influences
sections.text:
🌊 Open Sea Overview & Key Influences Welcome to the Open Sea 
    

 
  The open sea is the largest ecosystem on Earth. It is vast and variable
  and includes ocean waters away from coastal limits and above the
  seafloor. The word  pelagic  refers to the open seas or oceans.
 

 
  Coastal and seabed habitats are associated with tangible geological
  surfaces. The open sea is different because it is primarily defined by
  intangible conditions that cannot be touched but strongly shape the
  organisms living there.
 

 
   Rocky Shores 
   Sandy Shores 
   Piers & Jetties 
   Shale Rock 
   Elkhorn Slough 
   Into the Deep 
   Kelp Forest 
   Monterey Bay Habitat 
 
 Primary Open-Sea Influences 
    

 
  The training notes identify temperature, light and color, pressure,
  oxygen, salinity, nutrients, currents, sound, marine debris, and animal
  deception or camouflage as important open-sea topics.
 

 
  The source document provides detailed material for the dropdowns below.
  Marine debris was listed as a future topic but did not include supporting
  details, so no unverified debris section has been added.

References and source notes 

 
   
     Primary content source:  User-provided document,
    “zoom - open seas.docx.”
   

   
     Original app source:  User-provided Open Sea HTML
    exhibit reference.
   

   
    Numerical values and physiology statements are presented as volunteer
    training notes. They should be checked against current
    Aquarium-approved materials before formal publication or public use.
   

   
    No external photographs or third-party image assets are used in this
    version. Emoji are used as interface markers.
